items.title: Rational root certificate
items.note: Differs from the article lemma: "(D:rho) holds" refers to companion/chapters/12_D.tex:99-102, ρ = 129R/(V(U+129)) ≃ 0.060199206107543764815373666287 (the article's art:seed_rho asserts 0.060 < ρ < 0.061). Read as: at every point of the closed box (‖x − r̄‖∞ ≤ 10^-30, Vec 2 carries the sup norm) the denominator V(U+129) is positive and |129R/(V(U+129)) − 0.060199206107543764815373666287| < 10^-30/2 (nearest rounding to the printed thirty digits). Proved from the library: contraction (exists_unique_root), coarse positivity (box_denominators_and_ratio) and the rational interval evaluation of ρ on the root box (DDisplayPrecision.raw_bounds_on_original_ball, corrected_interval). The label map art:seed_rho → D:rho of editorial/prepare_shared_appendix.py turned the article's claim 0.060 < ρ < 0.061 into the thirty-digit claim; the printed proof (lines 41-92) derived only 0.060 < ρ < 0.061 until 15 October 2026, when wording point W6 was applied: the proof now ends "The same interval rules on the root box give the thirty digits in \eqref{D:rho}" (see C/seed_certificate/proof/001).

The article proof (A/seed_certificate/proof/001) with renamed labels; its undisplayed steps are stated in the article module (see that item). Wording point W6 applied on 15 October 2026: the proof derived only 60/1000 < ρ < 61/1000 ("Multiplying positive endpoints ..."), the article's art:seed_rho and what Lemma D:root states (12_D.tex:104-106), not the thirty-digit value ρ ≃ 0.060199206107543764815373666287 that "(D:rho) holds" claims (a proof gap, also behind "certifies (D:rho)" at 12_D.tex:117); it now ends "The same interval rules on the root box give the thirty digits in \eqref{D:rho}" (a companion-only replacement in editorial/prepare_shared_appendix.py). That claim is true: Lean proves it on the whole box by rational interval evaluation of ρ on the root box (Companion.SeedCertificate.root_certificate; DDisplayPrecision.raw_bounds_on_original_ball, corrected_interval). "compare Rump [Theorem 13.3]": literature comparison only.

resolved_discrepancies.description: "The same interval operations give the value enclosures in that table." (seed_certificate.tex:190) is copied from the article (paper/appendices/seed_certificate.tex:191), where "that table" is Table art:trial_table, whose value column lists rational enclosures of 10^4 G. In the companion the table is the one of Section comp:trial_table (12_D.tex:205-218, an unnumbered tabular; the current values G(z₀), G(z₁), G(z₂) follow in the display 12_D.tex:219-222), and it lists twelve-digit decimals, no enclosures. Read literally, the interval operations of this section, which run on the query box comp:query_box, would give those decimals. They cannot: G(z₀) = g₀ᵀz₀ = (897/1024 − ρ(1−c))/(1−ρ) varies by about 4.4·10^-6 over the query box (∂G(z₀)/∂ρ ≈ 0.22, Δρ = 2·10^-5), so every enclosure valid on that box has width > 10^-6 (Lean counterexample: Companion.SeedCertificate.query_box_too_coarse). (On the much smaller root box the same rules do give the twelve digits, DDisplayPrecision.raw_bounds_on_original_ball, but the appendix never evaluates there, so the sentence is at best ambiguous.) What the operations on the query box give are rational enclosures of width at most 4·10^-4 of every current value G(z_j) and trial value G(z_j+αp_j) (Lean: Article.SeedCertificate.table_value_enclosures; widths and the values at the root: Companion.SeedCertificate.table_enclosure_widths). The twelve-digit decimals are nearest roundings of the actual values, proved separately in Lean (DDisplayPrecision.corrected_error; Ch12D.trial_table, Ch12D.starting_values).
